text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 share index weakened for the third straight session, laid low by a mix of interest rate worries, a declining Dow, weak futures and nerves ahead of the new government's July 2 budget. The leading share index closed 25.2 points lower at 4,657. It has dropped 125 points this week since reaching a record closing high Friday.

FRANKFURT - Electronic trade in German stocks ended with the IBIS DAX index in positive territory, matching the market closing level from earlier on in trade mostly driven by derivatives. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,730.27, down 11.21 points, or 0.30 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,730.56, up 9.38 points, or 0.25 percent.

PARIS - Stocks closed weaker after a day of relatively light trading amid investor caution ahead of Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's debut parliamentary policy speech Thursday. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,751.74, down 10.86 points, or 0.39 percent.

ZURICH - Massive gains in Novartis stock led Swiss stocks 1 percent higher to record levels, with the Swiss Market Index (SMI) ending above 5,400 points for the first time. The Swiss market index closed at 5,405.0, up 59.1 points, or 1.11 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed down, but losses were limited as the dollar-yen rate did not react much to the big rise in Japan's trade surplus for May, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,497.85, down 95.81 points, or 0.47 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended down but trimmed afternoon losses following a bout of late buying in utilities that lifted the Hang Seng Index up from its day's low of 13,999.69, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,203.89, down 103.26 points, or 0.72 percent.

SYDNEY - Stocks meandered downward, with the only highlight being a late annnouncement confirming the merger of the nickel operations of QNI Ltd. and South Africa's Gencor Ltd. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,673.4, down 8.3 points, or 0.31 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks ended mixed, but an enormous asset swap deal by broker SBC Warburg boosted turnover into record territory, dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said. The All-share index closed at 7,218.4, up 26.3 points, or 0.37 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,096.7, down 3.8 points, or 0.01 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,432.1, down 0.6 points, or 0.35 percent.
